Original author-hosted full text found a Simon effect with the cat but not without. Later both experiments showed Simon effects regardless of cat presence; authors suggest the nearby experimenter may have supplied a competing spatial reference, so this failure is contextual rather than a claim that cat effects never occur. Machine-linked Simon/Stroop review is unrelated.

effect_name: Hopelessness scores predict later suicide in psychiatric cohorts
effect_claim: Among patients hospitalized for suicidal ideation, baseline hopelessness scores were associated with suicide during five to ten years of follow-up.
effect_claim_quote: only the Hopelessness Scale and the pessimism item of the Beck Depression Inventory predicted the eventual suicides.
original_title: Hopelessness and eventual suicide: a 10-year prospective study of patients hospitalized with suicidal ideation
replication_title: Relationship between hopelessness and ultimate suicide: a replication with psychiatric outpatients
replication_target_quote: thus replicating a previous study with hospitalized patients.
outcome_quote: hopelessness, as measured by the Beck Hopelessness Scale, was significantly related to eventual suicide.
review_note: The canonical 1990 American Journal of Psychiatry report is an independent outpatient cohort; DOI 10.1176/foc.4.2.291 is its 2006 reprint and is deliberately not used. This is an observed association within the studied cohorts, not a clinical prediction rule.

effect_name: Speech context shifts identification of a later vowel
effect_claim: The formant pattern of an introductory sentence altered how listeners identified a later target word's vowel.
effect_claim_quote: the identification of the test word depends on the formant structure of the introductory sentence.
original_title: Information Conveyed by Vowels
original_journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
replication_title: "Please say what this word is": Linguistic experience and acoustic context interact in vowel categorization
replication_target_quote: The present study replicated the original with U.K. and U.S. listeners.
outcome_quote: While the direction of the perceptual shift was consistent with the original study, neither sample replicated the large effect sizes.
review_note: The canonical 2023 journal article used digitized original stimuli. Both listener samples showed the original direction but neither matched the magnitude; DOI 10.1121/10.0015938 is a preceding conference abstract and is deliberately not used.

effect_name: Women place more weight on prospective partners socioeconomic status
effect_claim: In photo-and-status partner profiles, women weighted potential partners socioeconomic status more heavily than men when evaluating relationships involving affection or marriage.
effect_claim_quote: women place more emphasis than men do on partners' SES in such relationships.
original_title: Effects of potential partners' physical attractiveness and socioeconomic status on sexuality and partner selection
original_authors: J. M. Townsend and G. D. Levy
replication_title: Looks and status are still essential: Testing the mate preference priority model with the profile‐based experimental paradigm
replication_target_quote: We address this gap by testing the MPPM using J. M. Townsend's profile-based experimental paradigm, which utilizes profiles comprising photos of pre-rated models to manipulate physical attractiveness as well as costumes and descriptions to manipulate social status.
outcome_quote: increasing SS had a stronger positive effect on women's versus men's judgments.
review_note: Later article cites Townsend and Levy (1990a), names DOI 10.1007/bf01542229 in references, and explicitly calls its profile paradigm a replication. Narrow sex difference in status weight succeeds; social status was more important than predicted for both sexes in Singapore. 2022 is print issue year. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (field audit top40).

effect_name: Age amplifies contextual word predictability effects in Chinese reading time
effect_claim: Older Chinese adults showed larger word predictability effects than younger adults in gaze duration and regression-path reading times, while skipping effects did not differ by age.
effect_claim_quote: word predictability effects in reading time measures sensitive to both lexical identification (i.e., gaze duration) and contextual integration (i.e., regression-path reading times) were larger for the older than younger adults.
original_title: Older adults make greater use of word predictability in Chinese reading
replication_title: A further look at ageing and word predictability effects in Chinese reading: Evidence from one-character words
replication_target_quote: Perhaps the clearest evidence to date comes from a recent Chinese study showing larger word predictability effects for older adults in reading times but not skipping rates for two-character words.
outcome_quote: Our results replicate the finding that older adults produce larger word predictability effects in reading times but not word-skipping, despite high skipping rates.
review_note: Later one-character-word study explicitly cites Zhao et al. (2019) and links the 2019 DOI, which studied two-character words. It reproduces the age-by-predictability reading-time effect and null skipping interaction. 2021 is print issue year. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (W3047327815).

effect_name: Men confess romantic love before women
effect_claim: Across studies of current and past romantic relationships, men were more likely than women to say I love you first.
effect_claim_quote: it is actually men who confess love first and feel happier when receiving confessions.
original_title: Let's get serious: communicating commitment in romantic relationships
original_authors: Joshua M. Ackerman, Vladas Griskevicius, and Norman P. Li
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Men say “I love you” before women do: Robust across several countries
replication_journal: Journal of Social and Personal Relationships
replication_target_quote: We aimed to replicate this sex difference in an online cross-national sample (seven countries, three continents), while testing for variation according to attachment style and environment (the national sex ratio).
outcome_quote: Men were more likely to confess love first in a relationship
review_note: Later article explicitly identifies Ackerman et al. (2011) and its DOI, adapts its love-confession questionnaire, and finds male-first confessions in six of seven national samples. Narrow confession outcome succeeds; original sex difference in happiness on hearing love did not replicate. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (W4213244060).

effect_name: Oral reading fluency varies by passage and not presentation order
effect_claim: Second-grade oral reading fluency estimates differed substantially across supposedly comparable DIBELS passages, without a detectable presentation-order effect.
effect_claim_quote: Estimates of oral reading fluency varied across the six stories (67.9 to 93.9), but not as a function of presentation order.
original_title: Form Effects on the Estimation of Students’ Oral Reading Fluency using DIBELS
replication_title: Evaluating Passage and Order Effects of Oral Reading Fluency Passages in Second Grade: A Partial Replication
replication_target_quote: This study examines passage and order effects on the estimation of ORF scores using a set of second-grade passages.
outcome_quote: Results indicate that passage effects were substantial, but order effects were small but significant.
review_note: Later title identifies a partial replication, publisher Crossref reference list cites original Francis et al. DOI, and both studies counterbalanced passage/order in second grade. Passage effect confirms; small significant order effect diverges from original null. 2018 is print issue year. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (W2770856851).

effect_name: Hijab use is associated with more positive body image
effect_claim: British Muslim women who wore the hijab reported more positive body image and less internalization of beauty ideals than nonwearers after adjustment for religiosity.
effect_claim_quote: Controlling for religiosity, women who wore the hijab had more positive body image, lower internalization of media messages about beauty standards, and placed less importance on appearance than women who did not wear the hijab.
original_title: Is the hijab protective? An investigation of body image and related constructs among British Muslim women
original_authors: Viren Swami, Jusnara Miah, Nazerine Noorani, and Donna Taylor
replication_title: The hijab as a protective factor for body image and disordered eating: a replication in French Muslim women
replication_target_quote: We examined differences in body image and disordered eating between Muslim women who do and do not wear the hijab in France, a nation marked by religious-based sartorial censorship.
outcome_quote: women who wore the hijab reported significantly lower weight discrepancy, body dissatisfaction, drive for thinness, social physique anxiety, internalisation of the thin and muscular ideals, and pressure to attain ideals from peers and the media
review_note: Later paper cites Swami et al. (2014), including the British sample and matching hijab/body-image contrast, in its introduction. French association also survives adjustment for religiosity and support from Allah; perceived discrimination was higher. Online publication 2017, volume assigned 2016. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (W2606742552).

effect_name: Psychopathy facets have opposing links to negative emotionality
effect_claim: The interpersonal-affective facet of psychopathy was negatively associated with negative emotionality, while its social-deviance facet was positively associated.
effect_claim_quote: the interpersonal-affective facet of psychopathy is negatively associated whereas the social deviance facet of psychopathy is positively associated with facets of NEM.
original_title: Psychopathy and negative emotionality: Analyses of suppressor effects reveal distinct relations with emotional distress, fearfulness, and anger-hostility.
replication_title: Amygdala reactivity and negative emotionality: Divergent correlates of antisocial personality and psychopathy traits in a community sample.
replication_target_quote: The overall findings replicate seminal observations on NEM in psychopathy by Hicks and Patrick (2006)
outcome_quote: Higher psychopathy scores were associated with lower NEM and lower amygdala reactivity, whereas higher APD scores were related to greater NEM and greater amygdala reactivity, but only after overlapping variance in APD and psychopathy was adjusted for in the statistical model.
review_note: The later paper directly cites Hicks and Patrick (2006) and extends the suppression pattern from incarcerated men using PCL-R facets to community participants using dimensional psychopathy/APD measures. Its supplemental factor-2 analyses also found positive NEM associations; instruments and sample differ.

effect_name: Type A student scores are associated with higher grades
effect_claim: Students with stronger Type A behavior scores had higher grade point averages.
effect_claim_quote: Type A students also had higher grade point averages.
original_title: Type A Behavior Pattern: Relationship to Variation in Blood Pressure, Parental Characteristics, and Academic and Social Activities of Students
replication_title: The JAS-T and Type A in Students: A Replication Note
replication_target_quote: replicating earlier findings.
outcome_quote: Type A students reported desiring and achieving significantly higher GPAs than Type Bs (p less than .05)
review_note: The later Rainey paper cites the exact Waldron et al. (1980) OpenAlex work and retests the student GPA association using JAS-T extreme groups. The later extracurricular-activity sex difference is a separate result.

effect_name: Testosterone gains predict better bargaining when cortisol falls
effect_claim: Rising testosterone accompanied higher bargaining earnings and relationship quality when cortisol fell.
effect_claim_quote: testosterone rises were associated with high earnings and high relationship quality, but only if cortisol dropped.
original_title: Dual-Hormone Changes Are Related to Bargaining Performance
replication_title: Cortisol and Testosterone in Leadership Practice
replication_target_quote: We replicated previous work by Mehta, Mor, Yap and Prasad in testing the dual-hormone hypothesis related to testosterone increase and cortisol decrease (Study 1)
outcome_quote: our findings do not provide evidence to support the dual-hormone hypothesis.
review_note: The later article cites the exact Mehta et al. (2015) study and repeats a face-to-face negotiation with hormone measurements. It reports no support for the testosterone-by-cortisol effect; the other leadership tasks are extensions.

effect_name: Comrey scales can be faked and validity keys detect faking
effect_claim: The Comrey Personality Scales can be deliberately faked, while their validity keys distinguish some instructed fakers from honest respondents.
effect_claim_quote: Thus, the CPS may be faked, but the detection keys seem rather effective even when Ss are aware of their existence and try to beat them.
original_title: Faking and Faking Detection on the Comrey Personality Scales
replication_title: Faking and Faking Detection on the Comrey Personality Scales: Replication and Extension
replication_authors: John R. Braun, Annette Iervolino, Rebecca Francis
replication_target_quote: Braun and Iervolino (1972) found that mean scores were significantly higher under faking vs standard instructions for the two validity scales
outcome_quote: In conclusion, the present results confirm those of the original investigation.
review_note: The 1973 result confirmed fakability and some detection utility, but the detection rate fell significantly from 71% to 54%; the effect claim is limited to some detection utility.

effect_name: External locus of control and dogmatism
effect_claim: People with a more external locus of control score higher on dogmatism than people with a more internal locus of control.
effect_claim_quote: external control varying positively with dogmatism and was significant
original_title: Relationship between Locus of Control and Dogmatism
original_authors: Randall A. Clouser, Larry A. Hjelle
replication_title: Replication of the Relationship between Dogmatism and Locus of Control
replication_authors: Martin F. Sherman, Roger J. Pelletier, Richard M. Ryckman
replication_target_quote: Clouser and Hjelle then described a small, but positive correlation
outcome_quote: The data yielded small, but significant Pearson rs between dogmatism and all three locus of control dimensions, as anticipated.
review_note: The 1973 study extended the original one-scale correlation to three Levenson locus-of-control subscales and reported positive, significant associations for each.

effect_name: Sex differences in death attitudes
effect_claim: In college-student questionnaires, men reported more thoughts about death and dying but less negative affect about death than women.
effect_claim_quote: The men were more likely than women to think about death and dying (this was so on 5 of the 6 relevant items) but had less negative affective reaction to death and dying
original_title: Re-Examination of Middleton's Data: Sex Differences in Death Attitudes
replication_title: Sex Differences in Attitudes toward Death: A Replication
replication_target_quote: Lester (1970) analyzed questionnaire data from college students published in 1936
outcome_quote: The differences in this study are similar to those of the previous report.
review_note: The 1970 original reanalyzed 1936 responses; the 1971 same-author replication used new 1970 students, finding the same directional pattern on four of six thinking items and four of five affect items, with smaller differences.

effect_name: Laterborn advantage in facial kinship detection
effect_claim: Laterborn people detect kinship among strangers from face images more accurately than firstborn people.
effect_claim_quote: later-borns surpassed firstborns in detecting kinship among strangers
original_title: Firstborns’ Disadvantage in Kinship Detection
replication_title: Birth Order Does Not Affect Ability to Detect Kin
replication_target_quote: The current study aimed to replicate previous studies with better suited methods to determine the effect of birth order on kin recognition.
outcome_quote: Kinship judgment accuracy was unaffected by rater birth order.
review_note: Both canonical first-publication DOIs are OpenAlex Psychology primary. Original 2010 paper finds laterborn advantage for detecting kinship among strangers from face photographs in populations of different ages and two countries. Preregistered 2019 conceptual replication used 109 raters, 132 sibling or unrelated child pairs, and mixed-effects modelling; it found no birth-order interaction with actual relatedness. Stimuli and task differ from the original parent-child / varied-kin matching tasks, so the negative result is specific to child sibling face-pair judgments. Machine-linked 2011 child kinship development paper is unrelated.

effect_name: Psychopathic traits and reduced COVID-19 prevention behavior
effect_claim: Primary and secondary psychopathy traits were associated with lower reported COVID-19 prevention behavior in the original online sample.
effect_claim_quote: Primary psychopathy, grandiose narcissism, secondary psychopathy and BPD were associated with less COVID-19 prevention behaviour
original_title: COVID-19 prevention behaviour is differentially motivated by primary psychopathy, grandiose narcissism and vulnerable Dark Triad traits
replication_title: Psychopathy and COVID‐19: Callousness, impulsivity, and motivational reasons for engaging in prevention behavior
replication_target_quote: Two direct replication studies were conducted to investigate the associations of psychopathic traits with engagement in COVID‐19 prevention behavior
outcome_quote: negative associations of emotional callousness and impulsivity with prevention behavior
review_note: The later paper cites the exact Blanchard et al. 2022 OpenAlex work and conducts two direct studies of psychopathy and prevention behavior. Its negative callousness/impulsivity associations support the broad original psychopathy link; the original narcissism/BPD and severity mechanisms were not retested here.

effect_name: Affective priming of target-word pronunciation without stimulus repetition
effect_claim: A positive or negative picture prime facilitates pronunciation of a target word with matching valence even when the target has not been repeated.
effect_claim_quote: Results show that affective priming of naming responses does not depend on stimulus repetition.
original_title: Affective priming of naming responses does not depend on stimulus repetition
replication_title: Evaluative Priming in the Pronunciation Task: A Preregistered Replication and Extension
replication_target_quote: A replication condition was a close replication of the study by Spruyt and Hermans (2008).
outcome_quote: the main effect of evaluative congruency was not significant, F(1, 195) = 1.47, p = .23
review_note: Later canonical DOI is OpenAlex Psychology primary; original canonical DOI is classified Neuroscience by OpenAlex although published in Canadian Journal of Experimental Psychology. Later preregistered adversarial collaboration contained close replication with original picture-prime and target-word method plus semantic-relatedness controls. Preregistered overall congruency and first-block no-repetition tests were nonsignificant (first-block p=.23; overall p=.27), average priming 0.9 ms, d=.08. Exploratory pooled analysis across original and two new datasets found a very small effect dependent on highly semantically related pairs; authors say little evidence for evaluative priming independent of semantic relatedness. Original 2014 erratum corrected appendix target words, not analyses or conclusions. Machine-linked 2007 SOA/congruency-proportion study is not the tested original.

effect_name: Speech synchronization ability has a bimodal population distribution
effect_claim: The speech-to-speech synchronization test separated participants into high and low synchronizers with a bimodal phase-locking distribution.
effect_claim_quote: participants’ PLVs yield a bimodal distribution
original_title: Spontaneous synchronization to speech reveals neural mechanisms facilitating language learning
replication_title: Replication of population-level differences in auditory-motor synchronization ability in a Norwegian-speaking population
replication_target_quote: Therefore, it is critical to assess the universality of the population-level distribution (indicating two groups rather than a normal distribution) across populations of speakers.
outcome_quote: Here we demonstrate that the previous results replicate with a Norwegian-speaking population, indicating that the test is generalizable beyond previously tested populations of native English- and German-speakers.
review_note: Later article directly cites Assaneo et al. 2019 as reference 1 and its first cohort used the same English-syllable SSS stimulus in native Norwegian speakers; a second cohort used Swedish syllables. Later abstract reports replication of the bimodal high/low distribution. Original result is in the primary author manuscript. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (W4390014069).

effect_name: Agency rather than communion predicts humanness attribution
effect_claim: In animated-target and face studies, agency manipulations systematically changed humanness ratings whereas communion manipulations did not.
effect_claim_quote: agency but not communion had systematic effects on the ratings of humanness.
original_title: Understanding dehumanization: The role of agency and communion
replication_title: A Cross-Cultural Replication on Humanness Attribution
replication_target_quote: We conceptually replicate previous studies by involving a population of English and Arabic speakers to test cross-cultural replicability of the effect and the contribution of sensorimotor systems in agency representation.
outcome_quote: Goal achievement versus failure but not movement trajectory increased agency and communion ratings, which in turn affected humanness, respect, and liking (Study 1 and Study 2).
review_note: Later full text explicitly identifies Study 2b of Formanowicz et al. 2018 as the conceptual replication target: successful barrier-crossing dots were judged more agentic and human. That positive agency result recurred, but the later communion pathway diverged from the original null communion result; hence mixed. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (W4312542285).

effect_name: Wife negative start-up predicts relationship dissolution
effect_claim: A wife beginning a newlywed conflict discussion with negative affect predicts later marital separation or divorce.
effect_claim_quote: Support was found for models of the husband’s rejecting his wife’s influence, negative start-up by the wife
original_title: Predicting Marital Happiness and Stability from Newlywed Interactions
original_journal: Journal of Marriage and the Family
replication_title: Generalizability of Gottman and Colleagues’ Affective Process Models of Couples’ Relationship Outcomes
replication_target_quote: The generalizability of Gottman et al.’s (1998) affective process models was examined
outcome_quote: neither men nor women’s negative start up was predictive of separation at T2
review_note: Both canonical first-publication DOIs are OpenAlex Psychology primary. The 1998 original abstract reports support for wife negative start-up predicting divorce in 130 newlywed couples. The 2007 explicit constructive replication examined 85 married or cohabiting young couples from at-risk backgrounds after about 2.5 years and found no prediction of separation from women’s negative start-up. Different age, marital status, risk background, discussion task/topic design, and follow-up length limit the null to generalizability rather than the original sample. The later paper found some other affective predictors of relationship satisfaction; this row is restricted to negative start-up and relationship status. Machine-linked 2004 naive emotion coding study is unrelated.

effect_name: Embedded grammar intervention improves complement clause production over control
effect_claim: In an in-person science camp for children with developmental language disorder, the grammar intervention arm gained more on complement clause production than active controls.
effect_claim_quote: The grammar group performed significantly better at post-test than the active control group (d = 2.5, p = 0.049) on complement clause probes
original_title: Teaching little kids big sentences: A randomized controlled trial showing that children with DLD respond to complex syntax intervention embedded within the context of preschool/kindergarten science instruction
original_authors: Amanda J. Owen Van Horne et al.
original_journal: International Journal of Language & Communication Disorders
replication_title: Learning science concepts alongside language goals: A telehealth replication of a randomised controlled trial examining whether children with developmental language disorder can learn vocabulary or grammar in combination with curricular science content
replication_target_quote: This study replicates the core active ingredients of McGregor et al. (2021) and Owen Van Horne et al. (2023) while extending the findings to a telehealth platform.
outcome_quote: The grammar and science-only arms did not differ from each other (p = .16, see Supplemental Materials, Table S1).
review_note: Later accepted manuscript identifies Owen Van Horne et al. (2023), DOI 10.1111/1460-6984.12882, as an original in-person RCT and matches children with DLD, science-curriculum teaching, grammar arm, and complement-clause endpoint. Both studies found science and grammar gains, but the original grammar-arm advantage over active controls did not recur in the shorter telehealth study: grammar and science-only arms were not significantly different. The later paper also cites McGregor et al. 2021 for its separate vocabulary arm. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (W4406145891).

effect_name: Sample-first advantage in receptive identification learning
effect_claim: Presenting an auditory sample before visual choices leads children to master receptive identification in fewer trials than presenting the visual choices first.
effect_claim_quote: All participants took fewer trials to meet the mastery criterion in the sample-first condition than in the comparison-first condition.
original_title: Order of stimulus presentation influences children's acquisition in receptive identification tasks
replication_title: Stimulus presentation order in receptive identification tasks: A systematic replication
replication_target_quote: The procedures of Petursdottir and Aguilar (2016) were systematically replicated
outcome_quote: quicker mastery in the sample-first condition (four of seven evaluations) than in the comparison-first condition (two of seven evaluations)
review_note: Both canonical article DOIs are OpenAlex Psychology primary; original DOI first appeared online in October 2015 and belongs to the 2016 volume. Original study found sample-first faster in every participant. Later systematic replication added prompted error correction after incorrect responses and found sample-first faster in four of seven evaluations, comparison-first faster in two, and one neither: directional majority support but not universal. Machine-linked 2012 picture-prompt paper tests a different manipulation.

effect_name: Video feedback improves sensitive limit-setting in parents of twins
effect_claim: The VIPP-SD video feedback intervention improves observed sensitive limit-setting by parents of twin children relative to control.
effect_claim_quote: The VIPP-SD intervention had a positive impact on the level of parents’ positive limit-setting in interaction with their preschool twins
original_title: Video-feedback promotes sensitive limit-setting in parents of twin preschoolers: a randomized controlled trial
replication_title: Replicating a randomized trial with video-feedback to promote positive parenting in parents of school-aged twins
replication_target_quote: The purpose of our preregistered study was to replicate the findings of the VIPP-SD randomized controlled trial with parents of preschooler twins (Euser et al., 2021)
outcome_quote: We did not find a significant effect of the intervention on sensitivity or sensitive discipline.
review_note: Both canonical study DOIs are OpenAlex Psychology primary. Original registered RCT among parents of 202 preschool-twin families showed improved observed sensitive limit-setting, but not general parental sensitivity. Preregistered RCT replication in parents of 257 school-aged twin pairs found no improvement in observed sensitive discipline or sensitivity, although attitude toward sensitivity improved. The child-age range and discipline observation task differ (original Don’t Touch vs later combined Do/Don’t), so failure is an age/task boundary rather than proof intervention lacks benefit elsewhere. Machine-linked 2016 DOI is the original trial protocol, not its results paper.

effect_name: Task feedback changes strategy representations and cue sensitivity
effect_claim: In the Building Sticks Task, feedback altered how participants represented the problem and their sensitivity to strategy base rates and cues.
effect_claim_quote: task representations can be influenced by feedback from the environment, producing changes in base rate and cue sensitivity.
original_title: Task representations, strategy variability, and base-rate neglect
original_authors: Marsha C. Lovett and Christian D. Schunn
replication_title: Task representation and individual differences affect strategy selection and problem-solving performance
replication_target_quote: The goal of this study was to directly replicate and extend the results of one experiment that was conducted to assess the predictions of this theory.
outcome_quote: The results of the study replicated all prior results including: (1) a salient feature of the task influences people's initial task representation, (2) people prefer strategies with higher base rates of success under a task representation, (3) people tend to drop features from the task representation that are found not to be useful, and (4) there are more representation and strategy changes when success rates are low.
review_note: Later paper explicitly identifies Lovett and Schunn (1999) Experiment 1 and uses the Building Sticks Task to directly replicate RCCL predictions. The original author-hosted OSF PDF is a scanned page image; its first-page abstract was visually inspected, confirming the effect quote verbatim. Later study abstract reports all four original predictions replicated. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (W4408581259).

effect_name: Three punishment-sensitivity profiles in Planets and Pirates
effect_claim: The Planets and Pirates task distinguishes sensitive people who avoid punishment from experience, unaware people who avoid it after explicit information, and compulsive people who persist despite both.
effect_claim_quote: we identified three phenotypes of punishment avoidance
original_title: A cognitive pathway to punishment insensitivity
original_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
replication_title: Replication of individual differences in the Pirates and Planets conditioned punishment task, but no correspondence to behavior in a non-clinical sample
replication_journal: Journal of Behavior Therapy and Experimental Psychiatry
replication_target_quote: Here, we replicate and extend their findings using a within-subjects design with a larger sample (N = 188)
outcome_quote: We replicated the three profiles
review_note: Both canonical first-publication DOIs are OpenAlex Psychology primary. Original 2023 PNAS paper identified Sensitive, Unaware, and Compulsive punishment-avoidance phenotypes across three experiments. Later article first appeared online February 2026 and reports replication of all three profiles in a larger N=188 nonclinical sample with an extended task. It found no association of profiles with obsessive-compulsive behavior, alcohol use, depression, or anxiety, an external-validity limit rather than failure of the exact three-profile effect. Machine-linked 2012 rumination and punishment-sensitivity paper is unrelated.

effect_name: Skilled typists prefer letter combinations typed with different fingers
effect_claim: In forced-choice liking judgments, typists preferred nonmeaningful letter combinations typed with different fingers over same-finger combinations more often than nontypists did.
effect_claim_quote: typists more frequently preferred letter combinations typed with different fingers to combinations typed with the same finger.
original_title: Letters from the heart: Affective categorization of letter combinations in typists and nontypists
original_authors: Van den Bergh, Vrana, and Eelen
original_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition
replication_title: Embodied Preference Judgments: Can Likeability Be Driven by the Motor System?
replication_target_quote: this paradigm was first used by Van den Bergh, Vrana, & Eelen, 1990
outcome_quote: skilled typists preferred those typed with different fingers. Novices showed no preference.
review_note: The later primary paper explicitly says its forced-choice letter-dyad paradigm was first used by Van den Bergh et al. 1990. Skilled typists again preferred different-finger dyads and novices showed no preference. Its separate motor-task manipulation probes mechanism; this pair codes the original preference effect. Later primary field Psychology (OpenAlex W2163239204).

effect_name: Skilled typists prefer letter combinations typed with different fingers
effect_claim: In forced-choice liking judgments, typists preferred nonmeaningful letter combinations typed with different fingers over same-finger combinations more often than nontypists did.
effect_claim_quote: typists more frequently preferred letter combinations typed with different fingers to combinations typed with the same finger.
original_title: Letters from the heart: Affective categorization of letter combinations in typists and nontypists
original_authors: Van den Bergh, Vrana, and Eelen
original_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition
replication_title: On the Elusive Nature of the Letters from the Heart Effect
replication_target_quote: The Letters from the Heart effect described by Van den Bergh, Vrana, and Eelen in 1990
outcome_quote: The effect was not clearly replicated in these studies and thus seems to be elusive.
review_note: The later primary abstract explicitly names Van den Bergh, Vrana, and Eelen 1990 and tests the same typist versus nontypist different-finger preference in five studies with new letter combinations. The authors report it was not clearly replicated. This is a distinct later test from Beilock and Holt 2007, which did find the preference effect. Later primary field Psychology (OpenAlex W1970279353).

effect_name: Attractive male raters give more positive attractiveness judgments
effect_claim: Among male judges, the judges’ own attractiveness is positively associated with the attractiveness ratings they give to other people.
effect_claim_quote: male judges showed assimilation effects
original_title: Judging Physical Attractiveness: Effects of Judges' Own Attractiveness
replication_title: Judging attractiveness: Biases due to raters’ own attractiveness and intelligence
replication_target_quote: We attempted to replicate and extend these findings
outcome_quote: attractiveness judgments made by men, but not women, correlated positively with their own self-perceived level of attractiveness (r = .51, p < .001)
review_note: Both canonical first-publication DOIs are OpenAlex Psychology primary. Original male assimilation effect was based on observers rating judges’ attractiveness and judges rating photographs; later conceptual replication used self-rated attractiveness and judgments after face-to-face interaction, finding r=.51 for men. Original female contrast effect was not reproduced with women’s self-rated attractiveness; this row is deliberately restricted to the male positive-association claim. Later article received 2014, appeared online January 2015; original year is 1975. Machine-linked 2009 competitive self-rating study is unrelated.

effect_name: Music reminiscence bump in older adults
effect_claim: Older adults remember more about popular songs from their youth than popular songs from other life periods.
effect_claim_quote: The older adults’ emotionality ratings were highest for songs from their youth; they remembered more about these songs, as well.
original_title: Music, emotion, and autobiographical memory: They’re playing your song
replication_title: The distribution of memories for popular songs in old age: An individual differences approach
replication_target_quote: We first aimed to replicate the finding that songs that were popular during people’s adolescence are remembered best.
outcome_quote: Participants recognized a greater amount of songs that had been popular when they were between 10 and 30 years old.
review_note: Later canonical DOI first published online in 2015 and is OpenAlex Psychology primary; original 1999 Memory & Cognition paper is OpenAlex Neuroscience primary but is a psychological song-memory experiment. Original study had older adults listen to 20-second popular-song excerpts across the twentieth century and found greater song memory for youth-era music. Later explicit replication used 90 German older adults, popular German chart clips from 1954-1997, and found more recognition for songs popular when listeners were ages 10-30. Original and replication song pools, cultures, and measures differ; this is a conceptual replication. Machine-linked 2008 self-image reminiscence-bump paper concerns autobiographical memories, not songs.

effect_name: Reliable metaphor norm ratings
effect_claim: Ratings of literary and nonliterary metaphors across psychological dimensions were reliable in the original norming sample.
effect_claim_quote: the mean ratings of the metaphors were reliable (average Cronbach alpha = 0.88)
original_title: Norms for 204 Literary and 260 Nonliterary Metaphors on 10 Psychological Dimensions
original_authors: Albert N. Katz, Allan Paivio, Marc Marschark, James M. Clark
replication_title: A 25-year replication of Katz et al.’s (1988) metaphor norms
replication_authors: Spencer J. Campbell, Gary E. Raney
replication_target_quote: we conducted a renorming of selected metaphors from the database on a new student population.
outcome_quote: the pattern of responses has remained highly consistent across time and populations.
review_note: The later study renormed selected metaphors after 25 years and found highly correlated ratings; the original measured internal reliability, not longitudinal stability.

effect_name: Adolescent self-concept and family functioning
effect_claim: Adolescent self-concept was strongly associated with perceived family functioning in the original clinic and nonclinic samples.
effect_claim_quote: there were strong relationships between the self-concept variables and the family functioning variables.
original_title: Parent and adolescent perceptions of family functioning: a comparison of clinic and non‐clinic families
original_authors: Patricia Noller, Mary Seth-Smith, Ruth Bouma, Robert Schweitzer
replication_title: Self-concept, family functioning and problem type: A replication and extension of a study of clinic and non-clinic adolescents
replication_authors: Terry V. P. Bowles, Barry J. Fallon
replication_target_quote: This study replicates and extends previous research into self-concept and perceptions of family functioning held by clinic and nonclinic adolescents (1).
outcome_quote: self-concept is linked to family functioning, the sex of the adolescent, and help seeking behavior.
review_note: The later paper cites Noller et al. 1992 as reference 1 and reports links between self-concept and family functioning, with a different sample and added problem-type analyses.

effect_name: Rapid response predicts eating-disorder treatment outcome
effect_claim: Patients who reduced binge eating early in treatment were more likely to achieve remission and improve on eating pathology than slower responders.
effect_claim_quote: Participants with rapid response were more likely to achieve binge remission and had greater improvements in overall eating pathology and depressive symptomatology than participants without rapid response.
original_title: Rapid response predicts treatment outcomes in binge eating disorder: Implications for stepped care.
original_authors: Robin M. Masheb, Carlos M. Grilo
original_journal: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology
replication_title: Rapid response is predictive of treatment outcomes in a transdiagnostic intensive outpatient eating disorder sample: a replication of prior research in a real-world setting
replication_journal: Eating and Weight Disorders - Studies on Anorexia Bulimia and Obesity
replication_target_quote: The current study aimed to replicate findings from randomized controlled research trials and inpatient samples, identifying treatment outcome predictors in a transdiagnostic ED IOP sample.
outcome_quote: RR was the only significant predictor of ED symptoms post treatment
review_note: The later primary paper cites Masheb and Grilo 2007 as reference 38. Its intensive outpatient transdiagnostic sample extends the original randomized binge-eating-disorder treatment context.

effect_name: PTSD intrusions match trauma-memory hotspots
effect_claim: Intrusive trauma images in patients with PTSD commonly matched moments of peak emotional distress in their trauma memories.
effect_claim_quote: There was a high degree of match reported between intrusive images and hotspots.
original_title: Intrusive images and “hotspots” of trauma memories in Posttraumatic Stress Disorder: an exploratory investigation of emotions and cognitive themes
original_authors: Emily A. Holmes, Nick Grey, Kerry A. D. Young
original_journal: Journal of Behavior Therapy and Experimental Psychiatry
replication_title: “Hotspots” in trauma memories in the treatment of post-traumatic stress disorder: A replication
replication_target_quote: to replicate a previous study in this area (Holmes, Grey, & Young, 2005).
outcome_quote: the vast majority of main intrusions are also a hotspot.
review_note: The later author-uploaded full text explicitly reports that its main results replicate Holmes et al. 2005, including the intrusion-hotspot match; the later abstract foregrounds the emotion and cognition results.

effect_name: Psychological closeness to suicide methods and risk
effect_claim: Greater psychological closeness to a suicide method was associated with higher suicidal intent in the original high-risk samples.
effect_claim_quote: lower psychological distance, but not physical distance, predicted suicidal intent
original_title: Brief measures of physical and psychological distance to suicide methods as correlates and predictors of suicide risk: A multi-study prospective investigation
original_authors: Megan L. Rogers, Melanie A. Hom, Ian H. Stanley, Thomas E. Joiner
replication_title: Assessing relations between psychological closeness to suicide methods and suicide risk in a community sample: A replication study
replication_authors: Megan L. Rogers, Erik J. Reinbergs, William D. Murley
replication_target_quote: Previous literature suggests psychological closeness to suicide methods may significantly predict suicidal intent and behaviors, particularly among high-risk populations.
outcome_quote: psychological closeness to suicide methods was uniquely related to suicide risk, above and beyond physical closeness to these methods
review_note: The original article appeared online in 2018 and in a 2019 journal issue. The later study tested the association in a broader community sample with covariate adjustment, not the original prospective prediction.

effect_name: Resilient, overcontrolled, and undercontrolled personality prototypes
effect_claim: Q-sort personality profiles fall into resilient, overcontrolled, and undercontrolled types with characteristic Big Five profiles.
effect_claim_quote: Three replicable personality types were identified in a sample of 300 adolescent boys and shown to generalize across African Americans and Caucasians.
original_title: Resilient, overcontrolled, and undercontrolled boys: Three replicable personality types
original_authors: Robins, John, Caspi, Moffitt, and Stouthamer-Loeber
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Resilient, overcontrolled, and undercontrolled personality prototypes in childhood: Replicability, predictive power, and the trait-type issue
replication_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_target_quote: Relations reported by R. W. Robins, O. P. John, A. Caspi, T. E. Moffitt, & M. Stouthamer-Loeber (1996) between these 3 patterns and the Big Five were fully replicated.
outcome_quote: Relations reported by R. W. Robins, O. P. John, A. Caspi, T. E. Moffitt, & M. Stouthamer-Loeber (1996) between these 3 patterns and the Big Five were fully replicated.
review_note: German preschool Q-sort profiles replicated the earlier US adolescent-boy three-type structure and its Big Five relations. Different ages, cultures, and sample composition; successful conceptual replication of the type-trait pattern, not an exact protocol repeat. Both canonical first-publication DOIs have OpenAlex Psychology primary field.

effect_name: Peer-led eating disorder prevention reduces risk factors
effect_claim: Two peer-facilitated sorority programs, cognitive dissonance and media advocacy, reduce eating disorder risk factors.
effect_claim_quote: Although both interventions had an effect, cognitive dissonance generally was superior at eight-month followup.
original_title: Peer-facilitated eating disorder prevention: A randomized effectiveness trial of cognitive dissonance and media advocacy
replication_title: Effectiveness of peer-led eating disorders prevention: A replication trial
replication_authors: Becker, Bull, Schaumberg, Cauble, and Franco
replication_journal: Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology
replication_target_quote: The aim of this study was to replicate and extend results of a previous trial that investigated the effectiveness of 2 peer-led eating disorders prevention interventions in reducing eating disorder risk factors in undergraduate women (C. B. Becker, L. M. Smith, & A. C. Ciao, 2006).
outcome_quote: Results indicate that both interventions reduced thin-ideal internalization, body dissatisfaction, dietary restraint, and bulimic pathology at 8 months, although higher and lower risk participants responded somewhat differently.
review_note: Corrects machine original from a 2005 sorority trial to the explicitly identified 2006 peer-facilitated trial. Original N=90 and later N=188 randomized sorority members to cognitive dissonance or media advocacy. Both programs had beneficial effects; later study reported both reduced four risk factors at eight months, with risk-level moderation (only cognitive dissonance benefited lower-risk participants). OpenAlex Psychology primary for both.

effect_name: Belief outweighs factual falsity in English lie judgments
effect_claim: In English speakers ratings of lie scenarios, a speakers belief that the statement was false mattered most, deceptive intent next, and factual falsity least.
effect_claim_quote: falsity of belief is the most important element of the prototype of lie
original_title: Prototype semantics: The English word lie
replication_title: Indonesians Do Not Believe in Lying: New Results of Replicating Coleman and Kay’s Study
replication_target_quote: By replicating Coleman and Kay’s study of Indonesian speakers, the present paper tries to answer the following research questions.
outcome_quote: the factuality of the statement is more important to Indonesians than belief.
review_note: Later study translated the Coleman and Kay scenario ratings to Indonesian speakers. Original author-uploaded full text reports belief above deception above factual falsity; the Indonesian response hierarchy instead places factuality above belief. DOI 10.1353/lan.1981.0002 is the original journal DOI; 10.2307/414285 is an alternate JSTOR DOI. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (https://openalex.org/W3038465382).

effect_name: Rumination worsens depressed mood while distraction improves it
effect_claim: In depressed participants, an eight-minute rumination exercise increased depressed mood whereas a distraction exercise reduced it; nondepressed participants showed little mood change.
effect_claim_quote: Depressed subjects in the rumination condition became significantly more depressed, whereas depressed subjects in the distraction condition became significantly less depressed.
original_title: Effects of rumination and distraction on naturally occurring depressed mood
replication_title: The effects of rumination, distraction, and gratitude on positive and negative affect.
replication_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_target_quote: Based on the format of the rumination and distraction conditions from Nolen-Hoeksema and Morrow (1993), we created the gratitude condition by using self-relevant statements focused on the positive aspects of one’s life.
outcome_quote: the negative effects of the rumination condition were stronger among people relatively higher in baseline depression (compared to the distraction condition).
review_note: Later five-study article explicitly adapts Nolen-Hoeksema and Morrow (1993) rumination and distraction scripts and reports a baseline-depression interaction in the original direction. The provisional 1995 Lyubomirsky paper addressed negative interpretation/problem solving and is not the direct mood effect target. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (https://openalex.org/W4295899939).

effect_name: Transient mood influences global life satisfaction ratings
effect_claim: Participants induced into a good mood by recalling a happy event or interviewed on a sunny day rated their overall happiness and life satisfaction higher than those in a bad mood.
effect_claim_quote: In both experiments, subjects reported more happiness and satisfaction with their life as a whole when in a good mood than when in a bad mood.
original_title: Mood, misattribution, and judgments of well-being: Informative and directive functions of affective states
original_authors: Norbert Schwarz and Gerald L. Clore
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: The effect of mood on judgments of subjective well-being: Nine tests of the judgment model.
replication_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_target_quote: Studies 1 through 3 were designed to be fairly close replications of Study 1 in Schwarz and Clore (1983).
outcome_quote: Most of the 9 studies resulted in nonsignificant effects on life satisfaction and happiness judgments, and those that were significant were substantially smaller than effects found in previous research.
review_note: Later paper explicitly identifies studies 1-4 as close/direct replications of Schwarz and Clore (1983) Study 1 (happy/sad life-event writing), plus conceptual follow-ups. Most tests were null; a few smaller effects appeared, so mixed. Provisional 1987 Schwarz paper studied related mood effects but was not the direct writing-study original. 2016 is online publication year. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (https://openalex.org/W2561321161).

effect_name: Prediction errors boost adult novel-word retention
effect_claim: Adults retained novel word-object associations better when the novel word violated a stronger prior expectation.
effect_claim_quote: adults formed stronger memory traces for novel words that violated a stronger prior expectation.
original_title: Prediction error boosts retention of novel words in adults but not in children
original_authors: Chiara Gambi, Martin J. Pickering, and Hugh Rabagliati
replication_title: Do Children (and Adults) Benefit From a Prediction Error Boost in One-Shot Word Learning?
replication_target_quote: to check if Gambi, Pickering, et al.’s (2021) findings for English adults would replicate with a new set of materials.
outcome_quote: Moreover, we also failed to replicate previous evidence for such an effect in adults.
review_note: Later paper explicitly translates/adapts Gambi, Pickering et al. 2021 materials and tests two Italian-speaking adult samples for the same prediction-error boost. Original English adult positive effect did not replicate; child findings are separate. Provisional Greve et al. paper tested scene-item declarative memory, not the word-learning replication target. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (https://openalex.org/W4390816760).

effect_name: Free walking improves originality over constrained walking
effect_claim: Participants walking freely generated more original divergent-thinking responses than participants confined to a rectangular walking path or seated.
effect_claim_quote: the originality scores of participants in the free-walking condition were significantly higher than those of participants in the rectangular-walking and sitting conditions
original_title: Embodied metaphors and creative “acts”
replication_title: Sensorimotor-Conceptual Integration in Free Walking Enhances Divergent Thinking for Young and Older Adults
replication_target_quote: Leung et al. (2012) showed that participants who walked freely inside a square box performed better on divergent thinking than participants who walked along a rectangular path around the square box.
outcome_quote: Only the free-walking group showed better performance in fluency, flexibility, and originality.
review_note: Later article explicitly says Experiment 1 adopts the free-versus-rectangular walking conditions of Leung et al. 2012, especially its Study 2b; the originality difference recurred. The provisional Oppezzo 2014 study compared walking with sitting and was not the matched original. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (https://openalex.org/W2528436038).

effect_name: Skilled typists prefer letter combinations typed with different fingers
effect_claim: In forced-choice liking judgments, typists preferred nonmeaningful letter combinations typed with different fingers over same-finger combinations more often than nontypists did.
effect_claim_quote: typists more frequently preferred letter combinations typed with different fingers to combinations typed with the same finger.
original_title: Letters from the heart: Affective categorization of letter combinations in typists and nontypists
original_authors: Van den Bergh, Vrana, and Eelen
original_journal: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition
replication_title: Motor Fluency and Preference Judgments: Typing Speed as a Predictor of Letter Dyad Likeability
replication_authors: Mara Stockner, Giuliana Mazzoni, Francesco Ianì
replication_target_quote: A seminal study by Van den Bergh et al. (1990) has shown that expert typists, when presented with fluent and nonfluent letter combinations in a forced-choice paradigm, preferred more frequently fluent dyads.
outcome_quote: slow participants showed a preference for fluent dyads, while fast participants did not.
review_note: Conceptual later test of the same different-finger versus same-finger dyad preference. The 1990 study used forced-choice judgments and compared typists with nontypists. Stockner et al. presented individual dyads for oral yes/no likeability and split 30 modern typists by speed, with no nontypist group. Slow typists preferred fluent dyads (.63 versus .45), but fast typists did not (.53 versus .57); the dyad-by-speed interaction was significant. The supported subgroup reverses the original skill pattern.

effect_name: Gambling involvement correlates with antisocial behavior
effect_claim: Across measures in male students, greater gambling involvement was associated with more antisocial behavior.
effect_claim_quote: All forms of gambling and antisocial behavior were significantly correlated.
original_title: An Examination of the Relationship Between Gambling and Antisocial Behavior
replication_title: Gambling, Risk-Taking, and Antisocial Behavior: A Replication Study Supporting the Generality of Deviance
replication_target_quote: We conducted a replication (and extension) of two previous studies examining whether high frequency gambling is part of the generality of deviance
outcome_quote: The results of the present study largely replicate those previously found
review_note: The later paper says it replicates and extends two earlier studies and explicitly cites Mishra et al. 2011a, the original DOI here, as one of them. The original found gambling and antisocial measures correlated in 180 male students; the later community sample (n=328) reports largely replicated, often stronger associations. This row concerns that shared association, not every predictor in either paper. Both article dates use first online publication (2010 and 2016); journal issue years are 2011 and 2017. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology.

effect_name: Self-attention and expectancy interact on task persistence
effect_claim: After failure, self-directed attention amplifies persistence when success is expected and withdrawal when failure is expected.
effect_claim_quote: both of these tendencies would be mediated by self-directed attention. Results support the predictions.
original_title: Reassertion and giving up: The interactive role of self-directed attention and outcome expectancy
original_journal: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
replication_title: Experiments important to Carver and Scheier’s self-regulation theory are not replicable
replication_target_quote: With favorable expectations of success, participants low in self-awareness should be less persistent (measured by time until explicitly giving up an intractable task) than participants high in self-awareness. The opposite should be true for unfavorable expectancy.
outcome_quote: various theory-consistent ways of manipulating expectancies and self-awareness as well as subtracting periods of mental disengagement from time on task did not yield this predicted interaction.
review_note: The original 1979 two-experiment paper reports that expectancy effects on persistence depended on self-directed attention. The later paper explicitly tested this interaction in four experiments (N=45, 53, 40, 60), finding no predicted interaction. The later authors frame this as a test of four prior Carver-group studies, so this DOI anchors one original member of that evidence family. Both papers OpenAlex Psychology primary.

effect_name: First romantic partnership and reduced neuroticism
effect_claim: Entering a first romantic partnership is associated with a subsequent decline in neuroticism in young adulthood.
effect_claim_quote: higher neuroticism predicts the beginning of partner relationships and decreases once relationships are formed.
original_title: Relationships Matter in Personality Development: Evidence From an 8-Year Longitudinal Study Across Young Adulthood
replication_title: Long-Term Effects of Social Investment: The Case of Partnering in Young Adulthood
replication_target_quote: entering into the first long-term romantic relationship was accompanied by decreases in facets of neuroticism, thereby fully replicating findings by Neyer and Lehnart (2007) based on a German longitudinal study.
outcome_quote: entering into the first long-term romantic relationship was accompanied by decreases in facets of neuroticism, thereby fully replicating findings by Neyer and Lehnart (2007) based on a German longitudinal study.
review_note: Corrects machine original (Lehnart and Neyer 2006 stable/change partnership study) to the exact Neyer and Lehnart 2007 German first-partnership study named by the 2010 paper. Original author manuscript states neuroticism decreases once a first partnership is formed. Later used US Michigan longitudinal data and found decreases in neuroticism facets; observational association, not causal proof. Both later and original OpenAlex Psychology primary.

effect_name: Acute testosterone reduces cognitive reflection
effect_claim: A single testosterone dose lowers men’s Cognitive Reflection Test scores relative to placebo.
effect_claim_quote: Testosterone administration reduced CRT scores.
original_title: Single-Dose Testosterone Administration Impairs Cognitive Reflection in Men
replication_title: Does Testosterone Affect Cognitive Reflection? Evidence From a Double-Blind, Randomized Controlled Study of 1,000 Participants
replication_target_quote: Prior research has suggested that testosterone administration impaired CRT performance, but follow-up studies produced null results.
outcome_quote: We found an insignificant treatment effect on the CRT, with the point estimate in the opposite direction of the original hypothesis
review_note: Corrects machine original from Knight et al. 2020 commentary to the original Nave et al. 2017 RCT. Later preregistered adversarial collaboration randomized 1,000 men to intranasal testosterone or placebo and found no negative CRT effect (β logit 0.118, 95% CI −0.099 to 0.335). It used a modified seven-item CRT and a different testosterone administration paradigm from the original, so conceptual rather than exact replication. Both papers OpenAlex Psychology primary.

effect_name: Three sensory-processing sensitivity groups
effect_claim: Latent-class analyses of adult sensitivity scores identified low-, medium-, and high-sensitivity groups.
effect_claim_quote: people fall into three distinct sensitive groups along a sensitivity continuum.
original_title: Dandelions, tulips and orchids: evidence for the existence of low-sensitive, medium-sensitive and high-sensitive individuals
replication_title: Replication of the three sensitivity groups and investigation of their characteristics in Japanese samples
replication_target_quote: Studies in Western countries have suggested that people fall into the three sensitivity groups, namely high-, medium-, and low-SPS groups
outcome_quote: A series of latent class analysis indicated that the three-class model fitted best with the data.
review_note: The later article directly tests whether Western three-group sensitivity findings replicate in two Japanese university samples (N=1,257 and N=720) and cites Lionetti et al. 2018, whose adult study identified the low/medium/high classes. It also cites Pluess et al. 2018 on children; Lionetti is the closer adult original here. The later paper reports the three-class model fit best in both Japanese samples. This is a cross-cultural conceptual replication using the Japanese version of the scale. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology; the original is a Translational Psychiatry article.

effect_name: Pre-recognition skin response to taboo words
effect_claim: Before recognizing them, viewers show a stronger galvanic skin response to taboo words than to neutral words.
effect_claim_quote: The observers reacted with GSR's of significantly greater magnitude during the pre-recognition presentation of the critical words
original_title: Emotionality and perceptual defense
replication_title: Perceptual Defense, a Replication
replication_target_quote: McGinnies' (1949) study on perceptual defense was replicated.
outcome_quote: No significant results were noted for galvanic skin responses.
review_note: The original McGinnies study found stronger galvanic skin responses before recognition of emotionally toned/taboo words, plus higher recognition thresholds. The 1984 direct replication found no significant galvanic-skin-response effect, although the threshold difference did replicate; this row targets only the failed physiological effect. Corrects machine original from Erdelyi 1974 review to McGinnies 1949 primary experiment. Both OpenAlex Psychology primary.

effect_name: Facial cues shift war and peace leader preferences
effect_claim: Masculine-looking leaders are favored in war scenarios, whereas feminine-looking leaders are favored in peace scenarios.
effect_claim_quote: masculine-looking leaders are selected during intergroup conflict (war) and feminine-looking leaders during intergroup cooperation (peace).
original_title: Warriors and Peacekeepers: Testing a Biosocial Implicit Leadership Hypothesis of Intergroup Relations Using Masculine and Feminine Faces
original_authors: Spisak, Dekker, Krüger, and van Vugt
replication_title: Context-specific effects of facial dominance and trustworthiness on hypothetical leadership decisions
replication_authors: Ferguson, Owen, Hahn, Torrance, DeBruine, and Jones
replication_target_quote: Here we sought to replicate these effects using images of women’s faces, as previous studies have primarily focused on perceptions of leadership abilities from male faces
outcome_quote: more trustworthy-looking faces were preferred in leaders during times of peace and more dominant-looking faces were preferred in leaders during times of war.
review_note: Later full text explicitly identifies Spisak et al. 2012 as the conceptual replication target. Original experimentally morphed facial masculinity/femininity and tested leader choice in war/peace; later used naturally varying female faces rated for dominance/trustworthiness and tested the same context-specific direction. Masculinity/dominance and femininity/trustworthiness are related but different cues, so conceptual replication only. Both OpenAlex Psychology primary. Machine original (an individual-differences dominance study) was unrelated.

effect_name: Anticipated attractive partner increases women’s red display
effect_claim: Women expecting to interact with an attractive man display more red than women expecting a less attractive man.
effect_claim_quote: women who expected to interact with an attractive experimenter were substantially more likely to display red than those who expected to interact with an unattractive experimenter
original_title: Strategic Sexual Signals: Women's Display versus Avoidance of the Color Red Depends on the Attractiveness of an Anticipated Interaction Partner
replication_title: Antecedents of the red-romance effect: Men’s attractiveness and women’s fertility
replication_authors: Agthe, Niesta Kayser, Schwarz, and Maner
replication_target_quote: The current research is a reasonably powered conceptual replication designed to strengthen this literature by testing whether women are more inclined to display the color red
outcome_quote: Only the latter hypothesis received mixed support (mainly among women on hormonal birth control)
review_note: Later full text explicitly names the 2016 Niesta Kayser/Agthe/Maner study and says it used the same core experimental protocol, with an added no-photo control and fertility factor. Original N=74 found attractive-versus-unattractive man effect on red display (OR 6.78). Later N=281 found more red when expecting an attractive man, but this effect reached significance unexpectedly only in women using hormonal contraceptives; separate fertile-window hypothesis was null. Same senior team but independent samples. Both OpenAlex Psychology primary. Machine original about men rating red clothing in young vs menopausal women was the wrong link.

effect_name: Small reward increases favorable task attitudes after counterattitudinal compliance
effect_claim: After telling another person that boring tasks were enjoyable, participants paid one dollar rated the tasks more favorably than participants paid twenty dollars.
effect_claim_quote: The greater the reward offered (beyond what was necessary to elicit the behavior) the smaller was the effect.
original_title: Cognitive consequences of forced compliance
original_authors: Leon Festinger and James M. Carlsmith
original_journal: Journal of Abnormal and Social Psychology
replication_title: Attitude Change After Rewarded Dissonant and Consonant Forced Compliance: A Critical Replication of the Festinger and Carlsmith Experiment
replication_target_quote: l'auteur reprend l'sexperience de Festinger et Carlsmith, en y ajoutant des conditions
outcome_quote: fait apparaître une liaison inverse entre grandeur de la récompense et changement d'attitude, non seulement lorsque l'obéissance est dissonante, comme c'est le cas de l'expérience originale, mais également lorsque l'obéissance est consonante.
review_note: Nuttin explicitly critically replicates Festinger and Carlsmith, observing the inverse reward-attitude pattern in both dissonant and consonant compliance conditions. The original pattern recurs, but its dissonance-specific interpretation does not. The later publisher abstract does not report statistical significance for the dissonant condition; label mixed rather than unequivocally successful. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (https://openalex.org/W1935203897). Exact original and later DOIs absent from local FORRT archive and raw CSV registers.

effect_name: Inclusive-teaching self-efficacy is associated with teacher resilience
effect_claim: Among Finnish pre-service teachers, efficacy for inclusive teaching was the strongest variable related to perceived resilience.
effect_claim_quote: pre-service teachers’ self-efficacy was the strongest variable that related to their resilience.
original_title: Pre-service teachers’ self-efficacy in implementing inclusive practices and resilience in Finland
original_authors: Akie Yada, Piia Maria Björn, Pirjo Savolainen, Minna Kyttälä, Mikko Aro, and Hannu Savolainen
replication_title: Replicating the pathways to resilience: demographic predictors, self-efficacy, and inclusive teaching among pre-service teachers
replication_target_quote: This investigation replicates and extends prior inquiry by Yada et al. (2021) in a distinct socio-cultural setting
outcome_quote: Consistent with the Finnish study, this investigation confirmed a potent positive association between pre-service teachers’ self-efficacy for inclusive practices and their self-rated resilience
review_note: Cross-national conceptual replication supports the core self-efficacy-resilience association, while demographic predictors diverged. Later abstract incorrectly says original n=150; the original university repository abstract says n=105. Claim is associational, not causal. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (https://openalex.org/W4415363705). Exact original and later DOIs absent from local FORRT archive and raw CSV registers.

effect_name: Volunteer motivation scales align with autonomous and controlled factors

This is a broader conceptual replication, with different cohorts and measurement. Both OpenAlex primary field Psychology. No causal gene claim is inferred.

Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology (https://openalex.org/W319148433).

effect_name: U-shaped oxytocin and trust association in men

effect_name: Chewing gum and lower perceived stress in worker surveys
