outcome_quote: Data from 12 labs across the globe ( N = 1,775) revealed a small and significant ego depletion effect, d = 0.10.
review_note: Preregistered 12-lab N=1,775 Stroop-then-antisaccade conceptual replication; small positive pooled effect. Protocol retests Dang et al. 2017 rather than original 1998 sequence. No original-paper author. Psychology-primary.

effect_name: Attention control reduces subsequent working memory span
effect_claim: Ignoring distracting words during video viewing lowers subsequent working memory span relative to unrestricted viewing.
effect_claim_quote: Four experiments revealed that controlling the focus of visual attention (Experiment 1), inhibiting predominant writing tendencies (Experiment 2), taking a working memory test (Experiment 3), or exaggerating emotional expressions (Experiment 4) undermined performance on subsequent tests of working memory span, reverse digit span, and response inhibition, respectively.
original_title: Attention control, memory updating, and emotion regulation temporarily reduce the capacity for executive control
replication_title: No Evidence of the Ego-Depletion Effect across Task Characteristics and Individual Differences: A Pre-Registered Study
replication_authors: John Lurquin, Laura Elizabeth Michaelson, Jane E. Barker, Daniel E. Gustavson, Claudia C. von Bastian, Nicholas P. Carruth, Akira Miyake
replication_target_quote: we used the actual video material and verbatim instructions from the popular video-viewing attention control task employed by prior researchers.
outcome_quote: Contrary to the ego-depletion hypothesis, participants in the depletion condition did not perform worse than control participants on the subsequent self-control task, even after considering moderator variables.
review_note: Correction of the previously curated broad Baumeister 1998 link. Lurquin et al. 2016 directly retested Schmeichel 2007 Experiment 1: six-minute video, attend to interviewee and ignore on-screen words versus unrestricted control, followed by operation-span working memory. Preregistered N=200; no depletion effect, with slightly better nonsignificant scores in depletion. Later article cites Schmeichel 2007 as reference 5 and thanks Schmeichel for materials; he is not a later coauthor. Replaces one existing page, with no new counted pair. Cached OpenAlex W2274591123 primary Psychology.

replication_authors: Hause Lin, Blair Saunders, Malte Friese, Nathan J. Evans, Michael Inzlicht
replication_target_quote: An initial high-demand task reliably elicited very strong effort phenomenology compared with a low-demand task. Afterward, participants completed a Stroop task.
outcome_quote: However, our demand manipulation did not affect subsequent inhibition, as assessed with traditional Stroop behavioral measures and additional diffusion-model analyses for conflict tasks.
review_note: Four preregistered within-subjects N=686 conceptual tests: high initial effort changed response caution but did not impair subsequent Stroop inhibition. Mixed because process-level decision caution moved while original task-performance prediction failed. Psychology-primary.

original_title: Examination of the relation between an assessment of skills and performance on auditory–visual conditional discriminations for children with autism spectrum disorder
effect_name: Prerequisite skills predict auditory–visual discrimination training
effect_claim: A prerequisite-skills assessment predicts which children with autism will master auditory–visual conditional discrimination training.
effect_claim_quote: We compared the outcomes of the assessment to the results of auditory–visual conditional discrimination training and found that training outcomes were related to the assessment outcomes for 7 of the 9 participants.
replication_target_quote: The current study replicated the skills assessment developed and evaluated by Kodak et al. (2015) with 8 participants with ASD who received behavior analytic intervention that included at least 1 goal related to AVCD training.
outcome_quote: In addition, 5 participants' responding failed to reach mastery during subsequent exposure to AVCD training, which further demonstrated the predictive utility of the skills assessment.
replication_authors: Kodak, Bergmann, Cordeiro, Bamond, Isenhower, and Fiske
review_note: Independent eight-child ASD sample reused the 2015 five-skill prerequisite assessment before new AVCD training; predicted subsequent mastery failures. Same first author, new participants. Psychology-primary OpenAlex.
replication_title: Replication of a skills assessment for auditory–visual conditional discrimination training

original_title: Does a prosocial decision in video games lead to increased prosocial real-life behavior? The impact of reward and reasoning
original_authors: Iten, Bopp, Steiner, Opwis, and Mekler
effect_name: In-game helping, rewards, and later donation
effect_claim: Voluntary in-game helping predicts greater charitable donation, and the absence of an in-game reward promotes moral reasoning, prosocial self-concept, and donation.
effect_claim_quote: The results of both studies indicate that voluntarily deciding to help in a video game subsequently led to increased donating behavior. Further, results of Study 2 revealed that the absence of a reward for helping in-game affected players’ reasoning for helping and positively influenced prosocial self-concept and donation.
replication_target_quote: We partially replicated and extended a prior study that showed an impact of in-game rewards on a post-game charitable donation.
outcome_quote: Moral Reasoning was positively associated with donation behaviour, successfully replicating some prior findings. However, in-game rewards did not affect reasoning or donation behaviour.
review_note: Independent preregistered game experiment, new game and participants; moral reasoning–donation association reproduced but reward effect failed. FLoRA calls the exact Iten 2018 pair mixed. Psychology-primary OpenAlex.
replication_title: Do videogame rewards influence players’ subsequent prosocial engagement? A preregistered partial replication study on the role of reward and reasoning

original_title: Baseline training sequence affects speed of emergent conditional discriminations
original_journal: Journal of the Experimental Analysis of Behavior
effect_name: Tact-before-intraverbal training benefits emergent discrimination
effect_claim: Learning tact labels before intraverbal relations improves later emergent visual conditional-discrimination performance relative to the reverse training sequence.
effect_claim_quote: On average, the TI group had significantly shorter reaction times than the IT group throughout all four test blocks, even when controlling for intraverbal retention, which was lower in the IT group.
replication_target_quote: We examined the replicability and generality of a previously reported training sequence effect on emergent conditional discriminations in the intraverbal naming task.
outcome_quote: Compared to the IT sequence, the TI sequence resulted in greater mean accuracy at test (Experiment 1), higher yields (Experiment 2), and shorter reaction times (Experiment 2).
replication_journal: Journal of the Experimental Analysis of Behavior
review_note: Independent cohorts compared tact-intraverbal versus intraverbal-tact sequences in vocal Experiment 1 and selection-based Experiment 2. The direct sequence advantage and conceptual RT advantage recur. Psychology-primary OpenAlex.
replication_title: Training sequence effects on emergent conditional discriminations: Replication and extension to selection‐based training

effect_claim: The association between family cultural consonance and later depressive symptoms differs by serotonin 2A receptor -1438G/A genotype, strongest for the A/A variant.
effect_claim_quote: In addition, the interaction between genotype and cultural consonance in family life was significant.
replication_target_quote: To replicate a previously identified gene-environment interaction between a genetic polymorphism in the serotonin 2A receptor and cultural consonance in family life in relation to depressive symptoms (Dressler et al., 2009).
outcome_quote: The previously identified gene-environment interaction was not replicated.
replication_authors: Dressler, Balieiro, de Araújo, Silva, and dos Santos
review_note: Original longitudinal community cohort N=144; later four-economic-strata sample N=402 tested the same 5HT2A × family cultural consonance interaction, found no significant genotype interaction. FLoRA codes this exact pair failed. Psychology-primary OpenAlex.
replication_title: The interaction of cultural consonance and a polymorphism in the 2A serotonin receptor in relation to depression in Brazil: failure to replicate previous findings

outcome_quote: Contrary to the ego depletion hypothesis, however, performance did neither suffer from prior self-control exertion, nor as a function of task duration.
review_note: Independent high-powered N=709 sequential-task conceptual test. Neither task order nor 2–16 minute duration yielded later performance decrement; perceived demand increased. Different tasks from 1998. PubMed author abstract, Psychology-primary.

effect_claim: Higher observed rumination during an early CBT session predicts higher clinician-rated depression symptoms at the end of treatment.
effect_claim_quote: Mixed model results indicated that greater intensity of in-session rumination during the initial treatment session predicted higher levels of subsequent clinician-rated depressive symptoms (p < .023).
replication_target_quote: Moreover, we sought to replicate our prior findings that evaluated if early-treatment in-session rumination predicted symptoms later in treatment [20].
outcome_quote: both measures of in-session rumination at the first CBT session had a strong, positive association with clinician-rated HAM-D symptom severity at the end of CBT (rs > .498).

replication_journal: Journal of Mood and Anxiety Disorders
review_note: Outcome restricted to independent ISLAND cohort N=17 (CBT after SSRI nonremission), recruited 2014–2019 versus original PReDICT 2007–2013. Later paper also re-rates PReDICT patients, which is excluded from this claim. ISLAND first-session observed rumination predicted end-of-CBT clinician-rated depression. Psychology-primary OpenAlex.
replication_title: Assessing in-session rumination during CBT for depression: Replication and further evaluation of an observational measure

original_title: Mind-body practices and the self: yoga and meditation do not quiet the ego, but instead boost self-enhancement
effect_name: Mind-body practice self-enhancement via self-centrality
effect_claim: Yoga and meditation boost self-enhancement through greater self-centrality of the practice.
effect_claim_quote: Self-enhancement was higher in the yoga (Experiment 1) and meditation (Experiment 2) conditions, and those effects were mediated by greater self-centrality.
replication_title: Mind-Body Practices and Self-Enhancement: Direct Replications of Gebauer et al.’s (2018) Experiments 1 and 2
replication_target_quote: We conducted preregistered replications of both of Gebauer et al.’s experiments.
outcome_quote: Our results supported Gebauer et al.’s original conclusions that mind-body practices increase self-enhancement. Although the self-centrality effects were not clearly replicated in either experiment, we found evidence that measurement and sampling differences may explain this discrepancy.
review_note: Two independent Canadian preregistered samples retested the German yoga (N=97) and meditation (N=300) protocols. The self-enhancement increase replicated, but the proposed self-centrality pathway was not clearly replicated, so the joint claim is mixed, agreeing with the older FLoRA paper-level verdict. Later OpenAlex primary field Psychology; no authors overlap with the original.

effect_name: Working memory moderates perceptual disfluency benefit
effect_claim: Hard-to-read learning text improves retention and comprehension only for learners with higher working memory capacity.
effect_claim_quote: The results revealed significant aptitude-treatment-interaction effects with respect to retention and comprehension.
replication_target_quote: perceptually disfluent texts facilitated retention and comprehension performance (but not transfer performance) only for learners with higher working memory capacity (WMC).
outcome_quote: we obtained null results for disfluency, WMC, and their interaction for all learning outcomes.
review_note: Preregistered independent direct replication with same materials and measures, 96 participants versus 47; positive retention/comprehension interaction did not replicate. Transfer null was reproduced but is outside coded positive effect.
replication_title: Is the perceptual disfluency effect moderated by working memory capacity? Direct replication of Lehmann et al. (2016)

original_title: Gender Differences in Receptivity to Sexual Offers
effect_name: Gender by sexual proposition interaction
effect_claim: Men are more likely than women to accept a stranger’s sexual invitation, while receptivity to a date invitation is similar.
effect_claim_quote: The great majority of men were willing to have a sexual liaison with the women who approached them. Women were not. Not one woman agreed to a sexual liaison.
replication_target_quote: Clark and Hatfield (1989) found that men were more willing than women to accept casual sexual invitations, whereas no significant gender differences were observed in responses to propositions for non-committal social activities.
outcome_quote: In both studies, men more readily than women accepted a sexual invitation from a stranger of the opposite gender. In contrast to the original study, the gender difference was independent of the type of proposition.
review_note: Two new preregistered naturalistic field samples total N=240 reproduce sex difference for sexual offers but not interaction with proposition type. Original 1989 publisher DOI is canonical despite 2008 online digitization.
replication_title: Gender differences in receptivity to sexual invitations: two naturalistic replication studies

original_title: Self-efficacy as a mediator in the relationship between self-oriented perfectionism and academic procrastination
original_journal: Social Behavior and Personality: an international journal

effect_claim: Higher self-oriented perfectionism was associated with less academic procrastination, with self-efficacy fully mediating this relationship.

replication_target_quote: we report a preregistered conceptual replication testing five hypotheses based on Seo's key findings
outcome_quote: We found no evidence of a bivariate relationship between self-oriented perfectionism and academic procrastination in either set of analyses. review_note: New direct-Psych root-next150 list index 2. Original Korean college students N=692; later independent OECD Prolific college sample N=575, disjoint authors. Preregistered conceptual replication with changed scales/language. Total negative relationship was absent while a small negative indirect path via self-efficacy remained; full-study outcome mixed. Later OpenAlex W4254835574 primary Psychology.

original_journal: Proceedings of the SIGCHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems

effect_claim: In original Experiment 1, early adverb learning blocked later verb-tense learning, and early verb-tense learning blocked later adverb learning.

outcome_quote: Our close replication did not confirm the initial study's findings due to performance following verb pretraining: Pretraining on verbs did not bias attention to verbs in subsequent use.

Adverb-pretraining effects persisted, but the original reciprocal verb-pretraining effect failed. Therefore combined bidirectional claim is mixed. First online 2025, issue 2026. Authors disjoint.
original_title: THE BOUNDS OF ADULT LANGUAGE ACQUISITION
replication_authors: McManus, Bayas, Kerschen, Khoruzhaya, Zhuang, Magnuson
replication_title: Revisiting Blocking Effects in Second Language Learning: A Close Replication of Ellis and Sagarra (2010b)

effect_name: Repetition supports incidental collocation learning
effect_claim: More encounters with collocations in a read-and-listen graded reader improved incidental learning; 15 encounters produced sizeable gains.
effect_claim_quote: the number of encounters has a positive effect on learning. If learners encounter collocations 15 times within a graded reader, sizeable learning gains may occur.
replication_target_quote: This multisite study replicates Webb, Newton, and Chang's (2013) study on the effect of repetition on incidental learning of multiword units (MWUs).
outcome_quote: In line with the initial study, we found a positive effect of repetition. However, the learning gains were smaller, and the number of repetitions needed was different.
review_note: Independent multisite university and secondary-school samples repeated 1/5/10/15 exposures with the graded reader. Positive repetition effect recurred, but gain magnitude and repetition threshold differed from original, so combined claim mixed. Original first online 2012, issue 2013. Authors disjoint.
original_title: Incidental Learning of Collocation
replication_title: Repetition and Incidental Learning of Multiword Units: A Conceptual Multisite Replication Study of Webb, Newton, and Chang (2013)

effect_name: Explicit versus implicit collocation learning from exposure
effect_claim: The original study found explicit collocation knowledge gains under all input conditions but no implicit priming gains.
effect_claim_quote: all conditions led to significant long-term gains in explicit form recall and recognition both for natives and nonnatives, while no condition facilitated implicit collocational priming effects either for natives or nonnatives.
replication_target_quote: Sonbul and Schmitt (2013) showed that exposure to second language (L2) collocations in reading texts can produce gains in explicit knowledge, but they found no evidence of gains in implicit knowledge.
outcome_quote: These results replicated Sonbul and Schmitt's findings for explicit knowledge and extended their findings for implicit knowledge.
review_note: Independent advanced ESL sample found explicit gains as original, but implicit knowledge appeared in the unenhanced reading-only condition, contrasting with original no-implicit result. Later treatment used repeated medical collocations across two days, so conceptual replication. Combined explicit-plus-implicit finding mixed. Original first online 2012, issue 2013. Authors disjoint.
original_title: Explicit and Implicit Lexical Knowledge: Acquisition of Collocations Under Different Input Conditions
replication_title: The Development of Implicit and Explicit Knowledge of Collocations: A Conceptual Replication and Extension of Sonbul and Schmitt (2013)

effect_name: Five-month-old infants respond to simple addition and subtraction outcomes
effect_claim: Five-month-old infants distinguished outcomes of simple addition and subtraction on small object sets, interpreted by the original as arithmetic competence.
effect_claim_quote: Here I show that 5-month-old infants can calculate the results of simple arithmetical operations on small numbers of items.
replication_target_quote: An experiment is reported which replicates the findings of Wynn (1992).
outcome_quote: Results support Wynn's interpretation that infants' responses are based on arithmetical ability.
review_note: Independent sample of five-month-old infants repeated Wynn’s violation-of-expectation addition/subtraction task. The published abstract explicitly reports replication and support for original interpretation; secondary conditions varied object identity. Authors disjoint.
original_title: Addition and subtraction by human infants
replication_title: Do infants understand simple arithmetic? A replication of Wynn (1992)

effect_name: Mortality salience increases preference for human-distinctness essay

replication_target_quote: In Experiment 2 of the study ‘I am not an animal: Mortality salience, disgust, and the denial of human creatureliness’
outcome_quote: In a replication of this experiment conducted with 128 volunteers, we did not observe evidence for a mortality salience effect.
review_note: Independent sample of 128 volunteers retested original Experiment 2 essay-evaluation mortality-salience effect, and found no evidence for it. The Royal Society Open Science published version is hosted by University of Barcelona. Original Study 1 disgust effect is outside this claim. Authors disjoint.
original_title: I am not an animal: Mortality salience, disgust, and the denial of human creatureliness.
original_authors: Goldenberg, Pyszczynski, Greenberg, Solomon, Kluck, Cornwell
replication_title: Are we truly special and unique? A replication of Goldenberg et al. (2001)

original_title: The neural signature of escalating frustration in humans
replication_title: Escalating frustration - A replication attempt and extension of Yu et al. (2014)
effect_name: Goal proximity and expended effort increase frustration after blocked reward
effect_claim: Closer proximity to a reward and greater effort already expended independently increased self-reported frustration when the reward was blocked.
effect_claim_quote: proximity and expended effort independently enhanced participants' self-reported desire to obtain the reward, and their self-reported frustration
replication_target_quote: we attempted to replicate the findings of Yu and colleagues (2014) using the same experimental procedure
outcome_quote: In line with the original study, both goal proximity and exerted effort increased participants' self-reported motivation in the task and frustration after being blocked.
review_note: New direct-Psych root-next150 list index 8. Original lab Experiment 1 included 27 male volunteers; later independent lab N=32 and disjoint authors. This entry covers only the pre-specified retrospective self-reported frustration and motivation effects, which later authors explicitly replicated. Their response-force measure was invalid due to technical problems, exploratory facial EMG was null, and original fMRI was not retested; no claim is made about those outcomes. Published 2024 version-1 DOI, later peer-reviewed v2 2025. Later OpenAlex W4400538798 primary Psychology.

effect_name: Spousal support gap by sex and support type
effect_claim: Early-married women reported larger desired than experienced emotional and esteem support gaps, with culture-specific differences.
effect_claim_quote: both American and Chinese women experience gaps with respect to emotional and esteem support
original_title: Effects of Sex, Culture, and Support Type on Perceptions of Spousal Social Support: An Assessment of the "Support Gap" Hypothesis in Early Marriage
replication_title: A Replication of Xu & Burleson (2001) “Effects of Sex, Culture, and Support Type on Perceptions of Spousal Social Support: An Assessment of the ‘Support Gap’ Hypothesis in Early Marriage”
replication_target_quote: we have endeavored to replicate Xu and Burleson’s (2001) research study
outcome_quote: Results from our study partially replicate Xu and Burleson’s (2001) original findings and provide general empirical evidence for the support gap hypothesis.
review_note: Direct article-level retest of the support-gap hypothesis in U.S. and Chinese married couples. Later abstract states partial replication without naming which specific support-type contrasts held, so outcome is mixed for the original family of findings. Original and later authors disjoint; later cached OpenAlex primary Psychology.

effect_name: Helper intention affects gratitude more than indebtedness
effect_claim: Benevolent rather than selfish helper intention increases gratitude, while indebtedness does not respond to helper intention.
effect_claim_quote: Participants felt significantly more grateful when the helper had benevolent intentions. Reactions of indebtedness did not vary as a function of helper intention.
original_title: The Effects of Helper Intention on Gratitude and Indebtedness
replication_title: Revisiting the effects of helper intentions on gratitude and indebtedness: Replication and extensions Registered Report of Tsang (2006)
replication_target_quote: we conducted a replication and extensions of studies 2 and 3 from Tsang, 2006
outcome_quote: We concluded a successful replication, that helping intent was more strongly associated with gratitude than with indebtedness.
review_note: Preregistered registered report directly retested Tsang 2006 Studies 2 and 3 with n=759. Both later gratitude effects and expected null indebtedness effects matched the original; original/later authors disjoint. Later cached OpenAlex primary Psychology.

effect_name: Expecting to teach improves golf-putting retention
effect_claim: Practicing golf putting while expecting to teach it improves later putting performance relative to expecting a test.
effect_claim_quote: Results revealed that expecting to teach enhanced learning, even after controlling for the amount of studying and practicing.
original_title: Expecting to Teach Enhances Learning: Evidence From a Motor Learning Paradigm
original_journal: Journal of Motor Learning and Development
replication_title: Expecting to teach a novel golf putting task did not enhance retention performance: A replication attempt of Daou and colleagues
replication_target_quote: this study sought to replicate the expecting to teach effect
outcome_quote: The present study fails to replicate the benefits reported in the original experiments.
review_note: Preregistered golf-putting retest (n=76): retention radial error difference g=-0.13, 95% CI [-0.55,0.29], and no recall difference. Exact original 2016 published DOI confirmed by later article references; original/later authors disjoint; later cached OpenAlex primary Psychology.

original_title: Aiming at the same target: A masked priming study directly comparing derivation and inflection in the second language
replication_title: Comparing early-stage L2 processing of derived and inflected words: a conceptual replication of Jacob et al. (2018) with Chinese learners of L2 English
effect_name: L2 derived versus inflected masked morphological priming
effect_claim: Highly proficient Russian learners of German showed robust masked priming for derived German words but not inflected words.

replication_target_quote: a conceptual replication of Jacob et al.’s (2018) comparison of L2 early-stage processing of derived vs. inflected words
outcome_quote: showed qualitatively the same magnitude of priming in the derivational, inflectional, and form control conditions for Chinese learners of English
review_note: New direct-Psych root-next150 list index 3. Original masked priming sample 36 native Russian L2 German learners plus 40 German L1 controls; later independent Chinese L2 English learners and disjoint authors. Conceptual test of cross-language generalizability: latter found similar priming across derivation, inflection, and form-only controls, rejecting original qualitative derivation-versus-inflection distinction in the new L1/L2 pairing. Original online 2017/print 2018; later published 2025. Later cached OpenAlex primary Psychology.

original_title: Highly proficient L2 speakers still need to attend to a talker’s mouth when processing L2 speech
replication_title: Language proficiency modulates listeners’ selective attention to a talker’s mouth: A conceptual replication of Birulés et al. (2020)
replication_authors: Grüter, Kim, Nishizawa, Wang, Alzahrani, Chang, Nguyen, Nuesser, Ohba, Roos, Yusa
effect_name: Nonnative listeners attend more to a talker mouth irrespective of L2 proficiency
effect_claim: Second-language listeners fixated more on the talker’s mouth than native listeners, including highly proficient L2 listeners, with no modulation by L2 proficiency.

replication_target_quote: a conceptual replication of Birulés et al.’s (2020, Experiment 2) investigation
outcome_quote: Findings from one of the videos replicated results from the original study, showing greater attention to the talker’s mouth among L2 than L1 listeners. In both videos, L2 proficiency modulated attention, with more fixations on the mouth among lower proficiency listeners, an effect predicted but not observed in the original study.
review_note: New direct-Psych root-next150 list index 5. Later explicitly conceptually replicates original Experiment 2 with a different participant group, different listening materials, and disjoint authors. Original L2-versus-L1 mouth gaze difference held in one of two later videos; later observed proficiency modulation whereas original found none. Full-study outcome mixed. Later OpenAlex primary Psychology.

original_title: Comprehending and Learning From Internet Sources: Processing Patterns of Better and Poorer Learners
replication_title: Comprehending and learning from Internet sources: A conceptual replication study of Goldman, Braasch, Wiley, Greasser and Brodowinska (2012)

replication_target_quote: a conceptual replication of Goldman et al. (2012)

review_note: New direct-Psych root-next150 list index 6. Original n=21 US college L1 English readers (10 better, 11 poorer) reading seven web texts; later independent N=19 intermediate/advanced L2 German readers using five German web sources, disjoint authors. Later cached OpenAlex primary Psychology.

effect_name: Attention retraining reduces worry and threat bias

original_title: Attentional retraining: A randomized clinical trial for pathological worry
original_authors: Rebecca A. Hazen, Michael W. Vasey, Norman B. Schmidt
replication_title: The Efficacy of Attentional Bias Modification for Anxiety: A Registered Replication
replication_authors: Nathan Pond, Frances Meeten, Patrick Clarke, Lies Notebaert, Ryan Scott
replication_target_quote: conducting a replication of a seminal study showing successful alleviation of anxiety symptoms following multi-session ABM training (Hazen et al., 2009).

review_note: Registered independent replication used N=104 high worriers and five training sessions versus sham, following Hazen et al. (2009) N=24. It found no reduction in attention bias, worry, or trait anxiety; evidence for the depression outcome was insensitive. This finding concerns the tested probe-based intervention, not every anxiety treatment. Later published OpenAlex primary field Psychology.

effect_name: Lying about attitudes changes MFN and LPC responses
effect_claim: Directed lies about attitudes produced larger medial frontal negativity and smaller late positive ERP components than truthful responses.

original_authors: Ray Johnson, Heather Henkell, Elizabeth Simon, John Zhu
replication_title: Cognitive processes during deception about attitudes revisited: a replication study

outcome_quote: We obtained the same results as Johnson et al. (2008): lies were accompanied by enhanced medial frontal negativities (MFN) and suppressed late positive components (LPCs)
review_note: Independent German sample N=99 closely repeated Johnson et al. (2008) deception-about-attitudes ERP task and reproduced larger MFN and smaller LPC for lies, as well as reduced pre-response positivity. review_note: Third150 cached Psychology list index 20. Original Australian-born adults N=128 assessing apology for Japanese mistreatment of Australian POWs; later two independent Australian samples total N=1075 in the same intergroup apology context, disjoint authors. Later found no increase in apology desire, no reduction in sincerity or forgiveness, and little correlational support. Full-study failed. Later OpenAlex W7160704995 primary Psychology.

Later targets original Experiment 1 nonclinical university sample N=135, using independent Leuven psychology students N=238 analyzable and disjoint authors. Same classification stimuli, but depressive symptoms measured CES-D rather than original BDI; preregistered conceptual replication. Original Experiment 2 clinical patients were not targeted. effect_name: Attention retraining reduces depressive symptoms in dysphoria

replication_title: Biased attention retraining in dysphoria: a failure to replicate

replication_title: Revisiting the Temporal Pattern of Regret in Action Versus Inaction: Replication of Gilovich and Medvec (1994) With Extensions Examining Responsibility

original_title: Production and appreciation of humor as sexually selected traits
replication_title: Sex Differences in Preferences for Humor: A Replication, Modification, and Extension
effect_name: Sex difference in preference for a prospective mate's humor production versus receptivity

review_note: Cov index65. Many Labs 3 expressly names Stroop (1935) as the source and tests the core word-color interference with congruent versus incongruent trials. Across new multi-site participants, reaction-time interference replicated robustly (reported d=.88, t(3336)=50.22); all site estimates were significant and positive. The procedure used fewer colors and trials than Stroop's original and the paper explicitly expected a smaller effect. effect_claim: Macaques and baboons chose the larger quantity more accurately when the chosen items were separate from their food reward than when the chosen food items were themselves the reward.

review_note: Cross-species conceptual replication of the original monkey stimulus/reward separation test in a new sample of 12 Icelandic horses. review_note: Independent conceptual test of Vohs/Heatherton 2000 Study 3: Evers et al. 2010 explicitly cite it; their Study 3 randomized 62 women to suppress, reappraise, or naturally express emotion during a film before a taste test. Suppression produced greater comfort-food intake than natural expression (37.62 versus 21.95 grams; t(40)=2.76, p=.01, d=.85) and reappraisal, but not greater non-comfort-food intake. Unlike Vohs's original dieter subgroup, these were normal-weight students without eating pathology, so generalization is conceptual. No original/later author overlap. original_title: Feeding your feelings: Emotion regulation strategies and emotional eating
effect_name: Emotion suppression increases comfort-food intake
effect_claim: After an emotional film, instructed suppression raises comfort-food intake relative to no regulation, while reappraisal reduces intake relative to suppression.
effect_claim_quote: Relative to reappraisal and spontaneous expression, suppression led to increased food intake, but only of the comfort foods.
replication_title: Reappraise the Situation but Express Your Emotions: Impact of Emotion Regulation Strategies on ad libitum Food Intake
replication_target_quote: the control group ate less than the suppression group.
outcome_quote: whereas about two-thirds of the control (no ER instruction) and suppression groups began to eat, only one-third of the reappraisal group did.
review_note: Independent N=165 conceptual test explicitly comparing Evers et al. 2010 with a free-eating setting. As in Evers, suppression and reappraisal differed in total intake and eating initiation; however suppression and no-instruction control were essentially identical (75% versus 74.5% initiated eating; 10.56 versus 12.84 g total), whereas Evers had suppression > control. Among people who ate, ER instruction did not affect amount (F(2,97)=0.679, p=.509). The positive reappraisal effect and failed suppression-versus-control component justify mixed. Different procedure: freely optional snacking after two clips rather than forced taste test. No original/later author overlap. OpenAlex W2144157567 primary field Psychology.

effect_name: Anchor-consistent exemplar accessibility in lexical decisions
effect_claim: The original studies reported that comparing a target with a plausible numerical anchor selectively increased access to exemplar knowledge consistent with that anchor.
effect_claim_quote: Studies 1 through 3 demonstrate that comparing the target object with a plausible anchor (i.e., a standard that constitutes a possible value for the target) leads to a selective increase in the accessibility of anchor-consistent exemplar knowledge about the target.
replication_target_quote: Experiments 1 and 2 are large-sample (at least relative to the original sample sizes) replications of Studies 1 and 2 from Mussweiler and Strack (2000a), which are the studies using the proposed ‘signature test’ that are closest to prototypical anchoring studies.
outcome_quote: Four experiments were conducted to ascertain the evidence for selective accessibility with this test, tests that subsequently failed. A fifth experiment employed a different methodology, and again failed to show evidence for selective accessibility.
review_note: Cov index120. Later UCL-hosted accepted manuscript identifies Mussweiler & Strack 2000a by exact original title in its references and explicitly labels Experiments 1 and 2 replications of original Studies 1 and 2. It retests the lexical-decision signature of selective accessibility, not whether numerical anchoring itself exists; later authors emphasize anchoring remains robust. Original Study1 n28 and Study2 n30 in pre-Euro Germany; later n128 English-speaking UK participants in 2015/16, with language/material changes documented, plus further preregistered attempts. No author overlap (Thomas Mussweiler thanked for correspondence, not coauthor). Cached OpenAlex W2957689942 Psychology primary.

effect_claim: The original experiment reported that repeated finger flexion increased men's fun-seeking motivation and persistence relative to control, with a gender interaction.

review_note: Cov index16. The 2025 primary article explicitly calls Study1 a direct replication of Haeffel 2011 using the same equipment/tasks at the same university but newly recruited n216 undergraduates; Study2 is a conceptual replication in n246 adults recruited online.
